text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Non-oil exports dropped 7.9 percent in February, the fourth consecutive decline, suprising economists who had predicted an average increase of 1.5 percent rise.
- Umno Youth Leader Datuk Ahmad Zahid Hamid tells Singapore Foreign Minister S. Jayakumar not to "teach" Malaysia how to handle diplomatic ties.
- Ten members of two Malaysian human rights groups protested outside the Singapore High Commission in Kuala Lumpur against what they called "the vindictive persecution" of Singapore's opposition.
- The price war in the cellular phone industry has begun even as operators insist they have no intention of competing on price, ING Barings analyst Gautam Kapoor says.
- Mainboard-listed Parkway Holdings chalks up a full-year net earnings of Singapore $48 million, a 109 percent increase.
- FJ Benjamin shares suffer steep plunge to Singapore $90.5 cents compared to its previous day's close at Singapore $1.14.
- Pidemco Land and Raffles Medical Group plan to set up hospital in Blanco Court.
- Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan inched closer to calling for higher interest rates, saying tight labour markets were increasing inflation pressures

- In a bizarre twist to the Busang gold saga, Filipino geologist Michael de Guzman, who discovered the world's largest single gold deposit, fell off a helicopter deep in the Indonesian jungles and is presumed dead
- Kuok Brothers has offered M$7.50 each for shares in Perlis Plantations Bhd at Malaysian which iit does not own, valuing the company at Malaysian $2.7 billion.
- Natsteel Broadway Ltd net profits rose 33 percent to just over S$13 million.
- Indonesian Telecommunications carrier PT Telekom reported 65.8 percent rise in net earnings.
- Bread maker and supermarket operator QAF reported net profits of S$8.56 million for the nine months to December 31.
